title: Gate command timeout never applies after the gate verb rename
description:
The MCP server grants gate commands a ten-minute timeout, but the condition that selects them tests verbs the CLI no longer exposes, so every gate command runs under the default thirty-second timeout.

## Background

`getTimeoutForCommand` in the MCP server's CLI executor selects a long timeout for gate subcommands. Its condition compares the subcommand against `check`, `check-all`, and `pass`. The gate verbs are `evaluate`, `evaluate-all`, `status`, and `status-all`. No real command matches, so `jit gate evaluate` and `jit gate evaluate-all` are killed at the default timeout, well inside the window a checker script needs. The condition is also written so that only its first comparison is a comparison; the remaining operands are truthy string literals, which makes the branch depend solely on the first verb.

No test covers `getTimeoutForCommand`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Gate subcommands invoked through the MCP server run under the long timeout
- [hard] REQ-02: The timeout selection is driven by the CLI's current gate verbs
- [hard] REQ-03: A test asserts the timeout chosen for each gate verb and for a non-gate command
- [hard] REQ-04: The selection logic compares each candidate verb, so adding a verb cannot silently disable the branch
